issue.title: eth0 failed to get an IP address via DHCP when install the image via ONIE

failure.body:
#### Description

When installing an image from ONIE, it failed to get an IP address for eth0, which result in no way to access the DUT except console.  This issue can be reproduced from the master image with the latest commit hash c89567750.  As I tested, if I revert https://github.com/Azure/sonic-buildimage/commit/c8b5daed27fa29a1d993379d68dbbe5b05dcfc0d, this issue disappeared, so I believe this commit cause the issue.

This issue can be reproduced easily on different setups by simply install the image from ONIE,  and when it boots up, access through the console, manually issue command "dhclient eth0 -v" can have the IP address assigned correctly.

**No IP address assigned on eth0 after boot up:**

```

        inet6 fe80::<IPV6>  prefixlen 64  scopeid 0x20<link>
        ether <IPV6>  txqueuelen 1000  (Ethernet)

        TX packets 176  bytes 18674 (18.2 KiB)
        TX errors 0  dropped 0 overruns 0  carrier 0  collisions 0
        device memory 0xfb100000-fb1fffff
```

**relevant error observed in syslog:**


#### Steps to reproduce the issue:

1. Install an image via ONIE
2. Try to access the DUT via SSH, it will fail

#### Describe the results you received:

After installing the image from ONIE, no IP address was assigned to eth0

#### Describe the results you expected:

IP address should be assigned to eth0 and DUT should be accessible from SSH after boot up

resolution.title: ifupdown2: Don't check for new IP addresses if dhcp-wait is set to no
resolution.description:
Add a patch in ifupdown2 such that if DHCP is used for an interface, and
the policy setting sets dhcp-wait to no (meaning don't wait for dhclient
to acquire an IP address), then don't check to see if the interface has
a new IP address, since dhclient will still be working.

Fixes #8512.

Signed-off-by: Saikrishna Arcot <<EMAIL>>

#### Why I did it

SONiC ZTP (zero-touch provisioning) needs `dhcp-wait` to be set to `no` for ifupdown2, so that it won't wait for dhclient to get an address before moving on to the next interface. Since setting that policy then causes a failure (because of checks that ifupdown2 does to see if dhclient succeeded), add a patch to have it not check and see if dhclient succeeded or not.

#### How I did it

#### How to verify it

Within a KVM image:
1. Log into console.
2. Bring down eth0 using `sudo ifdown eth0`.
3. Edit `/etc/network/interfaces` so that `eth0` gets an address via dhcp, instead of being statically configured. Remove all of the lines in that section for static configuration.
4. On the host machine, start a DHCP server (dhcpd, dnsmasq, or similar), and have it listen on the br1 interface.
5. In the console connection, run `sudo ifup eth0`.
6. Verify that `eth0` has an IP address.
